title: McGill 1988: csa fibre corrected of transversus abdominis at L4-L5 (M, supine)
muscle_as_reported: Transverse abdominis (physiologic area from width; fibres parallel to scan plane)

imaging.plane: single transverse slice with the gantry tilted to the plane of the L4/L5 disc

quantity.name: csa_fibre_corrected
quantity.definition: anatomical CSA multiplied by cosine of fibre angle to the plane normal (authors may call it PCSA/physiological area; NOT volume/fibre-length PCSA); fibres run parallel to the scan plane; physiologic area estimated from muscle width (method in text)

source.authors: McGill SM, Patt N, Norman RW
source.sample: 13 active men; men referred for diagnostic CT (most with low back pain/sciatica), screened for activity level

how_to_simulate: Pose the model supine (lying; lordosis as when lying, no gravity load on trunk).
Select all transversus abdominis fascicles whose path crosses the plane at L4-L5 (single transverse slice with the gantry tilted to the plane of the L4/L5 disc), one side.
Sum their PCSA; use PCSA directly (fibre-angle corrected area).
Compare the one-side total with the measured mean +/- SD (bilateral sums are labelled side=bilateral_sum).

subject_model.source: Table 1 (SD age 11.9, height 5.9, weight 11.7); disc area 19.0 (2.4) cm2 Table 2
